description: An introduction to the internal organisation of a computer, focusing on the CPU and its parts, the system bus, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, the memory hierarchy and the von Neumann stored-program architecture.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the central processing unit (CPU) is responsible for directing and coordinating the operations of the computer?
mcq.explanation: The control unit (CU) manages and coordinates all activities of the CPU by fetching, decoding and directing the execution of instructions; the ALU only performs calculations and comparisons.

mcq.questionText: In which part of the CPU are arithmetic operations such as addition and logical comparisons performed?
mcq.explanation: The arithmetic and logic unit (ALU) carries out all arithmetic operations (add, subtract, etc.) and logical operations (such as comparisons of greater than, less than or equal to).

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of a register inside the CPU?

options.text: To store programs permanently when the computer is switched off
To hold small amounts of data temporarily during processing at very high speed
To connect the computer to the internet
To display output to the user

mcq.explanation: Registers are very fast, very small storage locations inside the CPU used to hold data, addresses or instructions that are being worked on at that instant.

mcq.questionText: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
mcq.explanation: The program counter (PC) always stores the memory address of the next instruction to be executed and is automatically increased after each fetch.

mcq.questionText: The instruction register (IR) is used to hold which of the following?

options.text: The address of the next instruction
The result of an arithmetic operation
The instruction that is currently being decoded and executed
The clock speed of the processor

mcq.explanation: The instruction register (IR) holds the current instruction that has just been fetched from memory so that the control unit can decode and execute it.

mcq.questionText: Which register temporarily stores the result of calculations carried out by the ALU?
mcq.explanation: The accumulator is a special register that temporarily holds the data being processed and the intermediate or final results produced by the ALU.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the system bus carries the location (address) of the memory cell that the CPU wants to read from or write to?
mcq.explanation: The address bus carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory, identifying the exact location to be accessed; it is one-directional.

mcq.questionText: Which type of system bus carries the actual information being transferred between the CPU and memory and is bidirectional?
mcq.explanation: The data bus carries the actual data and instructions between the CPU, memory and other devices and works in both directions (to and from the CPU).

mcq.questionText: What is the correct order of the steps in the machine (instruction) cycle?
mcq.explanation: The machine cycle follows the order Fetch (get the instruction from memory), Decode (interpret the instruction) and Execute (carry out the instruction).

mcq.questionText: Clock speed measured in gigahertz (GHz) tells us about which feature of the CPU?

options.text: How much data the storage can hold
How many cycles or pulses the CPU performs each second
How many colours the monitor can display

mcq.explanation: Clock speed is the number of cycles (pulses) the CPU can carry out per second; 1 GHz equals one thousand million cycles per second, so a higher clock speed generally means faster processing.

mcq.questionText: In the memory hierarchy, which type of memory is the fastest but also the smallest and most expensive per byte?
mcq.explanation: Registers are at the top of the memory hierarchy; they are the fastest to access but are very few and the most costly per byte, so they store only tiny amounts of data.

mcq.questionText: Which small high-speed memory sits between the CPU and main memory to store frequently used data and speed up processing?
mcq.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory placed between the CPU and RAM; it holds copies of frequently used instructions and data so the CPU can access them quickly.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly describes the difference between primary and secondary memory?

options.text: Primary memory is permanent storage while secondary memory loses data when power is off
Primary memory is directly accessed by the CPU and is mostly volatile, while secondary memory stores data permanently and is slower
Primary memory is always larger than secondary memory
There is no difference between them

mcq.explanation: Primary memory (such as RAM) is accessed directly by the CPU and is mostly volatile, whereas secondary memory (such as a hard disk) is slower, larger, cheaper and stores data permanently even without power.

mcq.questionText: According to the von Neumann architecture, the stored-program concept means that:

options.text: Programs are stored only on paper before use
Both program instructions and data are stored together in the same memory
Programs cannot be changed once written
Data is processed without using any memory

mcq.explanation: In the von Neumann (stored-program) architecture, both the instructions of a program and the data they use are held in the same main memory and fetched by the CPU as needed.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following would most improve the overall performance of a computer?

options.text: Reducing the clock speed of the CPU
Increasing the amount of RAM and using a faster CPU with more cache

mcq.explanation: Performance improves with a higher clock speed, more cores, larger cache and more RAM, because these reduce waiting and allow more data and instructions to be processed quickly.

fib.questionText: The two main parts of the CPU are the control unit and the _____ unit.
fib.explanation: The CPU is made up of the control unit (CU) and the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU), supported by registers.

fib.questionText: The register that always holds the address of the next instruction to be executed is called the program _____.
fib.explanation: The program counter (PC) keeps the address of the next instruction and is increased after each instruction is fetched.

fib.questionText: The three steps of the machine cycle are fetch, decode and _____.
fib.explanation: After an instruction is fetched and decoded, it is executed (carried out) by the CPU; this fetch-decode-execute sequence repeats continuously.

fib.questionText: The part of the system bus that carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory is the _____ bus.
fib.explanation: The address bus carries the address of the memory location to be accessed and is unidirectional (from CPU to memory).

fib.questionText: Memory that loses all its contents when the computer is switched off is described as _____ memory.
fib.explanation: RAM is volatile memory because it requires power to keep data; once power is removed, its contents are lost.

fib.questionText: The small, very fast memory placed between the CPU and main memory to speed up processing is called _____ memory.
fib.explanation: Cache memory stores frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU so they can be reached faster than from RAM.

fib.questionText: Read-only memory, which stores start-up instructions permanently and is non-volatile, is abbreviated as _____.
fib.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) holds permanent instructions such as the bootstrap (start-up) program and keeps its contents even when power is off.

fib.questionText: Inside the computer, all data and instructions are represented using the _____ number system, which uses only 0 and 1.
fib.explanation: Computers represent and process all data and instructions in binary (base 2), using the digits 0 and 1 to match the two states of electronic circuits.

fib.questionText: The architecture in which program instructions and data are stored together in the same memory is known as the _____ architecture.
fib.explanation: The von Neumann architecture introduced the stored-program concept, keeping both instructions and data in the same main memory.

fib.questionText: The speed of a CPU, measured as the number of cycles per second in hertz, is called the _____ speed.
fib.explanation: Clock speed, measured in hertz (commonly GHz), is the number of cycles the CPU performs each second; a higher value usually means faster processing.

tf.questionText: The control unit (CU) is the part of the CPU that performs arithmetic calculations such as addition and subtraction.
tf.explanation: Arithmetic calculations are performed by the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU); the control unit only directs and coordinates operations.

tf.questionText: Registers are storage locations found inside the CPU and are faster than RAM.
tf.explanation: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest storage in the memory hierarchy, faster than cache and RAM.

tf.questionText: The data bus is unidirectional, meaning data can only travel from memory to the CPU.
tf.explanation: The data bus is bidirectional; data can travel both from memory to the CPU and from the CPU to memory. It is the address bus that is unidirectional.

tf.questionText: During the fetch step of the machine cycle, an instruction is copied from memory into the CPU.
tf.explanation: In the fetch step the CPU uses the address in the program counter to bring (fetch) the next instruction from memory into the instruction register.

tf.questionText: A computer with a clock speed of 3 GHz performs fewer cycles per second than one with a clock speed of 2 GHz.
tf.explanation: A higher clock speed means more cycles per second, so a 3 GHz CPU performs more cycles per second than a 2 GHz CPU.

tf.questionText: Cache memory is larger and cheaper per byte than secondary storage such as a hard disk.
tf.explanation: Cache is small, very fast and expensive per byte; secondary storage like a hard disk is much larger and cheaper per byte but slower.

tf.questionText: ROM is non-volatile, so it keeps its contents even when the computer is turned off.
tf.explanation: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile and retains stored instructions, such as the start-up program, even without power.

tf.questionText: In the memory hierarchy, as you move from registers down to secondary storage, the storage capacity increases while the speed decreases.
tf.explanation: Moving down the memory hierarchy (registers, cache, RAM, secondary storage) gives larger and cheaper storage but slower access speeds.

tf.questionText: In the von Neumann architecture, program instructions and data are stored in completely separate memories that the CPU can never share.
tf.explanation: The von Neumann (stored-program) architecture stores both instructions and data together in the same main memory.

tf.questionText: Adding more RAM to a computer can improve its performance by allowing more programs and data to be held in main memory.
tf.explanation: More RAM lets the computer keep more programs and data in fast main memory, reducing the need to use slower secondary storage and improving performance.

summary.questionText: State the two main components of the central processing unit (CPU).
summary.correctAnswer: The control unit (CU) and the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU).
summary.explanation: The CPU is built around the control unit, which coordinates operations, and the ALU, which performs calculations and comparisons; registers support both.

summary.questionText: What is the role of the control unit (CU) in the CPU?
summary.correctAnswer: It directs and coordinates the operations of the computer by fetching, decoding and controlling the execution of instructions.
summary.explanation: The CU acts like a manager, sending control signals to other parts of the computer to make sure instructions are carried out in the correct order.

summary.questionText: Name the three buses that make up the system bus.
summary.correctAnswer: The data bus, the address bus and the control bus.
summary.explanation: The data bus carries data, the address bus carries memory addresses, and the control bus carries control and timing signals between the CPU and other parts.

summary.questionText: Briefly describe the three steps of the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
summary.correctAnswer: Fetch: the next instruction is brought from memory; Decode: the instruction is interpreted by the control unit; Execute: the instruction is carried out.
summary.explanation: This machine cycle repeats continuously while the computer runs, processing one instruction after another.

summary.questionText: List the levels of the memory hierarchy from fastest to slowest.
summary.correctAnswer: Registers, cache, RAM (main memory), then secondary storage.
summary.explanation: Speed decreases and capacity and cheapness increase as you move down from registers to secondary storage.

summary.questionText: Give one difference between RAM and ROM.
summary.correctAnswer: RAM is volatile and can be read from and written to, while ROM is non-volatile and is normally only read from.
summary.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is off and is used as working memory, while ROM keeps permanent instructions such as the start-up program.

summary.questionText: Why is cache memory used in a computer?
summary.correctAnswer: Cache memory stores frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU so they can be accessed faster than from RAM, improving performance.
summary.explanation: By keeping commonly needed items in very fast memory near the CPU, cache reduces the time the CPU spends waiting for data.

summary.questionText: Explain the stored-program concept of the von Neumann architecture.
summary.correctAnswer: It is the idea that both program instructions and the data they use are stored together in the same main memory, from where the CPU fetches them.
summary.explanation: Storing the program in memory allows the computer to be reprogrammed easily by simply loading different instructions.

summary.questionText: Why do computers represent all data and instructions in binary?
summary.correctAnswer: Because electronic circuits have two reliable states (on/off or high/low voltage) that match the two binary digits 0 and 1.
summary.explanation: Using only two states makes the circuits simple and reliable, so all data and instructions are coded as patterns of 0s and 1s.

summary.questionText: State three factors that affect the performance of a computer.
summary.correctAnswer: Clock speed, the amount of RAM, and the size of the cache memory (also the number of processor cores).
summary.explanation: A faster clock, more RAM, more cache and more cores all allow the computer to process data more quickly.

hoq.questionText: A student writes: "To make the CPU process data faster, the program counter should store the results of calculations." Why is this statement incorrect?

options.text: Because the program counter stores results, just like the accumulator does
Because the program counter holds the address of the next instruction, while results of calculations are held in the accumulator
Because the program counter is part of secondary storage
Because the program counter only works when the computer is off

hoq.explanation: The roles are different: the program counter keeps the address of the next instruction to fetch, while calculation results are held in the accumulator. Confusing these registers leads to the wrong conclusion.

hoq.questionText: Two computers have the same clock speed, but Computer A has 8 GB of RAM and a large cache while Computer B has 2 GB of RAM and no cache. Why is Computer A likely to perform better when running several large programs?

options.text: Because clock speed is the only factor that matters, so they perform the same
Because more RAM and a larger cache let Computer A keep more data close to the CPU, reducing waiting and slow access to secondary storage
Because Computer B has a faster hard disk that slows the CPU down
Because RAM and cache make no difference to performance

hoq.explanation: Performance depends on more than clock speed. More RAM allows more programs and data to stay in fast main memory, and a larger cache keeps frequently used items near the CPU, so Computer A waits less and runs faster.

hoq.questionText: During the fetch step of the machine cycle, the CPU must read an instruction from a specific memory location. Which registers and bus work together to make this happen?

options.text: The MAR puts the address on the address bus, then the fetched instruction returns via the data bus into the MDR
The accumulator puts the result on the control bus, then it returns via the address bus
The instruction register sends the clock speed to the data bus
The ALU calculates the address and sends it to secondary storage

hoq.explanation: The memory address register (MAR) places the required address on the address bus; the memory then returns the instruction along the data bus into the memory data register (MDR), from where it can be passed to the instruction register for decoding.
